rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makth means patient staying, lingering, or waiting; its lexical sense is not everlasting duration.
rows.anchor: المكث في اللغة: هو الأناة واللبث والإنتظار وليس بمعنى الخلود أصل المكث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a good reward is payment for work and precedes the Garden, makth suggests awaiting what follows the reward; it fits the context better than wording for eternal residence.
rows.anchor: الأجر الذي يُدفع مقابل العمل وننظر ماذا يحصل بعد الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an does not attribute evil to God, while it attributes blessings to Him; the author supports this with the contrast between bestowed favor and affliction by evil.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى لا ينسب السوء إلى نفسه؛ أما الخير والنِعم فكلها منسوبة إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says God gives life and takes it, but says “when I fall ill” and credits God with healing, as a mark of reverence.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل يمرضني تأدباً مع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “I intended” assigns the ship's damage to Khidr alone, since the defect was an evil act and God is not credited with it.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى لا ينسب العيب إلى نفسه أبداً فكان الخضر هو الذي عاب السفينة فجاء الفعل مفرداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual “we intended” covers Khidr's killing of the boy and God's replacement of him with a better child: the deed combines Khidr's harmful act with God's good act.
rows.anchor: في الآية إذن جانب قتل وجانب إبدال فجاء جانب القتل من الخضر وجاء الإبدال من الله تعالى لذا جاء الفعل مثنّى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall's restoration is wholly good, so its action is attributed to God alone; He knew the treasure lay beneath it and protected the orphan boys from villagers taking it unjustly if the wall fell.
rows.anchor: الجدار كلّه خير فنسب الفعل لله وحده وأنه يدلّ على أن الله تعالى هو علاّم الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title Rabb suits the passage because it means nurturer, teacher, guardian, and provider, matching its themes of care and upbringing.
rows.anchor: الرب هو المربي والمعلِّم والراعي والرازق والآيات كلها في معنى الرعاية والتعهد والتربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A village can be small or large; when it expands, it is called a city.
rows.anchor: إذا اتّسعت القرية تُسمى مدينة، والقرية قد تكون صغيرة وقد تكون كبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Yasin, the messengers' preaching reached the city's farthest point, and the man who came from its outskirts carried the burden of calling his people; this shows their effort despite the city's size.
rows.anchor: وصل التبليغ إلى أقصى نقطة في المدينة مع أنها متّسعة وهذا فيه دليل على جهدهم لنشر الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Khidr searched the extensive village and became so hungry that they asked its inhabitants for food.
rows.anchor: أي أنهما جالا فيها كلها وبلغ بهم الجوع كثيراً حتى استطعموا أهلها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators, including al-Zamakhshari, take the waw before “and their dog was the eighth” as circumstantial and as confirming that this is the correct count.
rows.anchor: كما صرّح المفسرون أي كأنها تدل على أن الذين قالوا أن أصحاب الكهف كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw is circumstantial and stresses verification: it appears when descriptions are semantically distant, but is omitted when the descriptions are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: الواو إذن هي واو الحال ولكنها أفادت التوكيد والتحقيق بأن هذا القول صحيح لأن الواو يؤتى بها إذا تباعد معنى الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates distant descriptions joined by waw with “the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden,” and similar descriptions without waw with “slanderer, going about with calumnies.”
rows.anchor: وإذا اقترب معنى الصفات لا يؤتى بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām after a verb of saying is not always for transmission: it can mean “about,” as in the cited poetic line, or introduce a cause.
rows.anchor: ورود اللام بعد القول له أكثر من دلالة وهو ليس دائماً للتبليغ وإنما تأتي لبيان العِلّّة إما بمعنى عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the poet's line, “they said to her face,” the lām means “about her face,” not that they spoke to her directly.
rows.anchor: قلن لوجهها بمعنى عن وجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “a word issuing from their mouths,” كلمة is a tamyiz explaining an implicit subject, a construction called the subject clarified by tamyiz.
rows.anchor: كلمة هي تمييز، الفاعل ضمير مستتر ويأتي التمييز ليفسرها وتسمى في النحو: الفاعل المفسّر بالتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أي is the subject and an interrogative noun; such sentence-initial words are not governed by what precedes them except a preposition, though what follows can govern them.
rows.anchor: أي: هي مبتدأ. وهي من أسماء الإستفهام وكل الأسماء التي لها صدر الكلام لا يعمل بها ما قبلها إلا حروف الجرّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to the exegetes, the definite ship was a passing boat the pair had not found earlier; its crew recognized Khidr and carried them without payment, while the boy was an unspecified child met on the road.
rows.anchor: حسب التفاسير أن الخضر وموسى - عليه السلام - لم يجدا سفينة لما جاءا إلى الساحل ثم جاءت سفينة مارّة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'y means running or brisk walking; ihsan is mastery rather than ordinary work. Fi'l can describe an inanimate thing, 'amal need not be skilled making, and sun' is finer, intentional work by a rational agent.
rows.anchor: والإحسان هو الإتقان وليس العمل العادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines misguidance, striving, and skilled making, so it fittingly says “greatest losers in deeds”; it is the Qur'an's only attribution of loss to work, in a passage framed throughout by deeds.
rows.anchor: جاء فيها ضلال وسعي وصُنع لذا استوجب أن يؤتى بكلمة الأخسرين أعمالاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-akhsarin is a comparative superlative: many are losers, and some are worse than others, so the ranking is among the losers themselves.
rows.anchor: الأخسرين: اسم تفضيل أي أنه هناك اشتراك في الخُسران، يوجد خاسرون كُثُر والأخسرين بعضهم أخسر من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra t in istaṭāʿa adds meaning and makes the verb suited to urging effort, consistent with the principle that increased form brings increased meaning.
rows.anchor: زيادة التاء في فعل استطاع تجعل الفعل مناسباً للحث وزيادة المبنى في اللغة تفيد زيادة المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Climbing the iron-and-copper barrier is easier than boring through it, so the shorter form is used for climbing and the full form for making a hole; deletion suits the lighter act, while the full form suits the hard, long act.
rows.anchor: الصعود على السدّ أهون من إحداث نقب فيه لأن السدّ قد صنعه ذو القرنين من زبر الحديد والنحاس المذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shorter pronunciation for climbing also matches its shorter duration, while the longer pronunciation matches the time-consuming act of making a hole.
rows.anchor: الصعود على السدّ يتطلّب زمناً أقصر من إحداث النقب فيه فحذف من الفعل وقصّر منه ليجانس النطق الزمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The t remains in the first verse because Khidr is explaining and clarifying, but is deleted in the second because it is the parting scene and he says nothing further before leaving Moses.
rows.anchor: المقام في الآية الأولى مقام شرح وإيضاح وتبيين فلم يحذف من الفعل أما في الآية الثانية فهي في مقام مفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an usually puts hearing before sight because hearing is more important for religious obligation and conveying a message: a blind person who hears can be reached, while a deaf person is harder to address.
rows.anchor: الأكثر في القرآن تقديم السمع على البصر لأن السمع أهم من البصر في التكليف والتبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing has a shorter range than sight, so a person we hear is usually closer than someone we see.
rows.anchor: مدى السمع أقل من مدى البصر فمن نسمعه يكون عادة أقرب ممن نراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing develops in a person before sight, another reason it is normally mentioned first.
rows.anchor: السمع ينشأ في الإنسان قبل البصر في التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sleepers hid in a dark cave to avoid being seen, yet God sees them there; they also told their companion to be discreet so the people would not see him, making sight the salient sense in this context.
rows.anchor: لجأوا إلى ظلمة الكهف لكيلا يراهم أحد لكن الله تعالى يراهم في تقلبهم في ظلمة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life the criminals heard about resurrection but did not see it, leaving room for doubt; in the afterlife they see what they had heard, reaching certainty, so that realm fittingly foregrounds sight.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا يسمعون عن القيامة وأحوالها ولا يبصرون لكن ما يسمعوه كان يدخل في مجال الشك والظنّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares the certainty of direct sight to the saying that hearing news is not like seeing for oneself.
rows.anchor: وكما يقال ليس الخبر كالمعاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tomorrow” in the verse need not mean the next calendar day; qad can indicate the future, fitting what happened and what will happen.
rows.anchor: غداً في الآية موضع السؤال لا تعني بالضرورة الغد أي اليوم الذي يلي وإنما (قد) تفيد المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damaging a plank in the ship to preserve it is less shocking than killing a boy without an apparent cause, so the milder word imr suits the ship and the harsher nukr suits the killing.
rows.anchor: خرق السفينة ونزع لوح خشب منها دون قتل الغلام شناعة فإنه إنما خرق السفينة لتبقى لمالكيها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says nukr is more severe than imr.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: النُكر أشدّ من الإمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each description fits its act; the two words would not be apt if exchanged.
rows.anchor: فجاء كل على ما يلائم ولم يكن ليحسن مجيء أحد الوصفين في موضع الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difference between imr and nukr also contributes to the verse-endings.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف يدخل في فواصل الآي في القرآن الكريم
